=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text tconst "magic constant: "
global grid ulong 81
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emitw writes n right-aligned in w columns (w at most 20; a wider number is not cut)
fn emitw n ulong w ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 32
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
if gt w sub 20 i
i = sub 20 w
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note the Siamese method: 1 goes in the middle of the top row; each next number goes one up and one
note right (wrapping round), or straight down when that cell is taken, which happens every n numbers
fn siamese n ulong to void
for i ulong mul n n
put grid i 0
end
r = ulong 0
c = div n 2
for k ulong mul n n
put grid add mul r n c add k 1
ur = rem sub add r n 1 n
uc = rem add c 1 n
if eq get grid add mul ur n uc 0
r = ur
c = uc
else
r = rem add r 1 n
end
end
end
fn show n ulong to void
for i ulong n
for j ulong n
emitw get grid add mul i n j 4
end
emit nl
end
emit tconst
emitu div mul n add mul n n 1 2
emit nl
end
fn main to int
siamese 3
show 3
emit nl
siamese 5
show 5
emit nl
siamese 9
show 9
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
